acceptance: Red test first: a boundary with a fake probe that reports agy exhausted writes the agy bench before the first lane admission.
A family whose probe fails is not benched and the boundary logs one WARN.
The wave status shows the benched families at launch.

consumed.resolution: The pre-wave probe of the loop (runPreWaveProbes, before the pool admits a lane) already probed every installed family at wave 145 launch and benched agy-claude; the Gemini group was not yet exhausted then (the agy scouts ran Gemini 3.8 Flash for 60+ actions). This change bounds that probe by cli_health.usage_evidence_timeout_s, makes a failed or late probe one WARN that benches nothing, and shows the active benches in evolve wave status. No second probe step was added to boundary run.

fix: At the boundary (evolve boundary run / wave next preflight), run the bridge usage probe for each family that cli_routing can pick, and bench each exhausted scope through the existing clihealth bench, before the pool admits a lane. A failed probe is a WARN and does not bench.
notes: Console route: boundary and bridge probes.
source: console, 2026-10-27, operator "investigate in watcher issue"; wave-145 errors channel 10:05Z-12:40Z (1387 WARN signals)
summary: Wave 145 launched at 10:05Z with agy at 100% weekly in both groups (Gemini resets in 143 h, Claude/GPT in 159 h). No bench existed, because the boundary probes only claude and a bench is written only after a lane exits 85 or someone runs the probe. All 4 first scouts (2058-2061) ran on agy and went busy-stagnant (LIVENESS_PANE_STAGNANT), and the router lost a launch to exit 85 (ADVISOR_LAUNCH_FAILED, c2059). A console usage probe at 12:5xZ then wrote the bench until 2026-10-28T18:53+08.
title: Each wave launch probes the usage of every routed family and benches an exhausted one before the first lane
